# Willpower @ Stage 2 — Irritability

> developed 2026-07-24.

## Crosswalk (from unified ladder)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| IST Stage# | 2 |
| Canonical name | Irritability |
| Altitude | `infrared` (Pre-egocentric) |
| MHC Order | 1 (Automatic) |
| Kegan | Pre-Kegan |
| Identity band | Pre-egocentric |

## Expression on this line

Willpower at Order 1 is biological self-regulation: homeostasis, immune response, stress
adaptation — the organism's automatic capacity to maintain internal stability in the face of
external perturbation. This is not willpower in the cognitive sense; it is the biological
substrate of all later self-regulation: the organism that automatically adjusts its internal
state to maintain equilibrium.

The key advance over Order 0 is that self-regulation now has a *directional quality* — the
organism actively corrects deviations from its set-point, not just passively maintains its
structure. This directional self-correction is the biological substrate of all later willpower.

## Integrity markers (healthy inclusion)

- **UL:** the felt quality of biological self-regulation — the organism that automatically
  corrects deviations from equilibrium.
- **UR:** reliable homeostatic self-correction — the organism consistently returns to its
  set-point after perturbation.
- **LL:** none — no shared self-regulatory framework.
- **LR:** the biological feedback mechanisms that enable self-correction.

## Pathology markers (Agape / Eros)

- **Dark addiction:** rigidity — the organism that cannot adapt its set-point, maintaining
  equilibrium at the cost of flexibility.
- **Dark allergy:** dysregulation — the organism that cannot maintain equilibrium, oscillating
  wildly without returning to set-point.
- **Golden addiction:** projecting cognitive self-regulation onto biological homeostasis.
- **Golden allergy:** denying that biological self-regulation is a legitimate willpower
  beginning.

## Diagnostic cues (Gross / Ground R&D)

- **Homeostatic self-correction:** the organism actively corrects deviations from its
  set-point.
- **Directional self-regulation:** the organism moves toward equilibrium, not just passively
  maintains structure.
- **Biological feedback:** self-regulation is driven by biological feedback mechanisms.

## Sources, joints, open questions

**Sources:** Cannon, *The Wisdom of the Body* (homeostasis as biological self-regulation);
McEwen, "Stress, adaptation, and disease: Allostasis and allostatic load" (*Annals of the
New York Academy of Sciences*, 1998).
**Open joints:** How does biological self-regulation shade into agentive self-control
(Order 2)?
**Research debt:** pairs with `01-prehension` (physical stability) and `03-basic-impulse`
(agentive self-control).
